name: Motorized Scooter
description: Any motor-powered vehicle or micromobility device on no more than three wheels, with or without a seat, that can't exceed 20 mph on level ground; an electric bike with a motor of 750 W or more fits the definition if it can't go faster than 20 mph. Defined by Florida Statutes §316.003(48) and regulated by §316.2128, last amended by chapter 2025-149.
restrictions: No more than three wheels, with or without a seat or saddle; pedals are optional
Can't propel it faster than 20 mph on level ground
A pedaled one rated at 2 brake horsepower or less also meets the moped definition, and the statutes don't say which governs
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration, title or insurance
Has a bicycle rider's rights and duties, and is exempt from the ban on motorized vehicles on sidewalks and bicycle paths
A local government may regulate it on streets, highways, sidewalks and sidewalk areas
Since July 1, 2025 a local government may set minimum ages by ordinance and require riders to carry government-issued photo ID
